10.1002_advs.202504094: Rationally modulating the reconstructed structure of electrocatalyst is an effective avenue toward selective electrochemical CO 2 reduction (e‐CO 2 RR). Herein, it is reported that a Ce‐incorporated Cu oxide (CeCuO x ) can have prominent performance for the selective production of C 2 H 4 with a high Faraday efficiency (FE) of 55.39% at −0.93 V, and partial current density of −39.50 mA cm −2 at −1.03 V, higher than those of Cu oxide and Cu at the same potential. Systematical experimental investigations show that the CeCuO x reconstructs to oxygen‐contained Cu with optimized Cu 0 /(Cu + +Cu 2+ ) ratio and electronic structure through Ce leaching and in situ reduction. All of those benefit water molecule cleavage and OH − accumulation that could provide hydrogen feedstock and suppress competitive hydrogen evolution. Importantly, specific C 1–2 intermediates generation and activation are enhanced, achieving high C 2 H 4 selectivity and efficiency. Our work provides new insights into the relationship between the reconstructed structure and mechanism for boosting CO 2 to multi‐carbon products.
10.1002_aenm.202501634: Anion exchange membrane (AEM) water electrolysis holds promise for green hydrogen production. One of the main challenges is the preparation of highly efficient electrodes with scalable techniques. Herein, a novel Fe‐modulating Raney‐Ni electrode (NFA‐CA) is developed through atmospheric plasma spraying and chemical etching techniques. The resulting electrode demonstrates high bifunctional catalytic activities with low overpotentials and Tafel slopes (HER: 27 mV at 10 mA cm −2 , 20 mV dec −1 ; OER: 169 mV at 10 mA cm −2 , 49 mV dec −1 ), competing for precious‐metal catalysts and leading transition‐metal‐based compounds reported in the literature. Moreover, the corresponding AEM electrolyzer only requires 1.56 V to drive 1 A cm −2 and exceptional durability for 1000 h. Moreover, the AEM cell can reach 2 A cm −2 at 1.79 V, exceeding the United States Department of Energy target for AWE systems (2 A cm −2 at 1.80 V). The highly efficient and durable performance is attributed to the NiFe nanocrystals (core)‐NiFe hydroxide (shell) nanostructures created by the treatment. This structure not only facilitates superior electrocatalytic properties but it is also maintained after 1000 h of continuous operation. It is consider that the present approach can offer an attractive route for scalable fabrication of NiFe‐based electrodes for industrial AEM water electrolyzers.
10.1002_anie.3824462: Electrocatalytic conversion of water‐soluble organics in aqueous media offers a sustainable route to high‐value chemicals, yet sluggish mass transport remains a critical bottleneck at industrially relevant current densities. Here, dimethyl sulfoxide (DMSO) is employed as the modifier to enhance mass transport by reconstructing hydrogen‐bond (H‐bond) networks. In the bulk electrolyte, DMSO inserts into the dense hydrogen bonds to expand the free‐volume distribution, releasing reactants from the solvation shell and accelerating their diffusion. Simultaneously, interfacial interactions between DMSO, reactants, and cations enrich local reactant concentrations, cooperatively facilitating the reaction kinetics. This dual‐enhancement mechanism achieves ∼60% Faradaic efficiency (FE) in electrocatalytic dehalogenative hydrogenolysis at 300 mA cm −2 . Our strategy demonstrates broad utility across the dehalogenative hydrogenation of other halogenated substrates and the hydrogenation of nitriles/nitro compounds, delivering >10% FE improvements. By coupling bulk diffusion acceleration with interfacial reactant enrichment, this work offers a promising strategy to overcome mass transport limitations in aqueous electrosynthesis.
10.1002_eem2.70367: The electrocatalytic sulfide oxidation reaction (SOR) has emerged as a promising strategy for removing reduced sulfur, owing to its low thermodynamic energy barrier and capacity to generate high-value products. However, current progress remains largely restricted to laboratory studies, and industrial-scale implementation is urgently needed to achieve effective sulfur pollution control and resource recovery. This review provides a comprehensive overview of recent advances in catalyst fabrication, reaction system engineering, and product acquisition, all of which offer opportunities to accelerate the industrial development of SOR. Particular attention is paid to the existence of diverse reduced sulfur species (S2-, HS-, H2S) under varying industrial conditions, as these strongly affect catalyst mechanisms and application feasibility. Building on this foundation, several catalyst design strategies are discussed to enhance catalyst stability and activity. Beyond catalyst design, emphasis is placed on coupling SOR with diverse cathodic reactions for integrated applications and on leveraging novel electrolytic devices to improve process efficiency. Pathways to high-value products are also highlighted, with a focus on diversifying product types and developing cost-effective recovery strategies. This review concludes by discussing current challenges and future opportunities, aiming to provide guidance for advancing SOR from laboratory research to sustainable industrial practice.
10.1016_j.chempr.2025.102460: The electrochemical synthesis of ammonia presents a promising pathway to decarbonize and electrify the production of the world’s second-largest commodity chemical. Among potential reactants, NOx gases stand out due to their favorable thermodynamics, advantageous kinetics, and availability from both combustion emissions and nitrogen-fixation processes, such as plasma-induced atmospheric nitrogen oxidation. However, the typically low concentrations of NOx in these sources poses significant challenges for electrochemical performance, particularly due to limitations in reactant mass transport. In this work, we report on the use of a porous nickel catalyst in a membrane electrode assembly (MEA) electrolyzer to enable the direct use of a dilute nitric oxide (NO) feed. The rational optimization of reactant mass transport enabled achieving a NO-to-NH3 single pass conversion of 93%, a faradaic efficiency for ammonia of 92% and an ammonium production rate of 557 μmol/h·cm2.
10.1016_j.xcrp.2026.103628: Photothermal membrane distillation (PMD) has emerged as a promising solar-driven desalination technology by enabling localized interfacial heating to overcome the energy limitations of conventional membrane distillation (MD). This review summarizes recent advances in photothermal membranes for MD applications, focusing on photothermal materials and membrane architectures. The roles of plasmonic metals, semiconductor nanostructures, carbon-based materials, conjugated polymers, MXenes, and metal-organic frameworks are discussed in terms of photothermal mechanisms, structure-property relationships, and design considerations. Membrane fabrication strategies, including surface coating, blending, freestanding structures, and hierarchical architectures, are evaluated regarding light absorption, heat localization, hydrophobicity, and vapor transport. Representative PMD membrane performances are compared, and key challenges including long-term stability, scalability, and standardized evaluation are highlighted. Future perspectives, such as additive manufacturing, hybrid systems, and data-driven optimization, are discussed to guide the development of practical PMD technologies.
10.1016_j.xinn.2026.101499: The ambitious goal of net-zero carbon emissions has driven an unprecedented expansion of global wind and solar power.1 Increasing reliance on these weather-dependent resources amplifies the variability in energy supply, exacerbating the supply-demand mismatches within power systems.2 To date, scientific and policy attention has focused disproportionately on the extreme energy deficit events, in which demand far exceeds supply, commonly termed “energy droughts.”3 However, the opposing extreme energy surplus events remain critically overlooked: periods of massive oversupply—energy floods.
10.1021_acsami.6c15279: Lead selenide (PbSe) thin films are attractive for room-temperature infrared photodetection, yet efficient self-powered operation relies on the construction of a high-quality heterojunction. Herein, an asymmetric Ag/PbSe/Ni electrode structure was fabricated and subsequently annealed in an O2 atmosphere, inducing Ag diffusion into the PbSe film and in situ phase conversion at the Ag/PbSe interface to form Ag2Se. As a result, a high-quality Ag/Ag2Se/PbSe/Ni heterojunction was directly constructed. Under zero bias and 1550 nm illumination, the device exhibits an ultralow dark current of 1.61 × 10-9 A, an Ion/Ioff ratio of 521, detectivity of 7.73 × 1010 Jones, and responsivity of 8.78 mA/W, demonstrating excellent self-powered infrared photodetection performance. Notably, the Ag electrode serves not only as an electrical contact but also as a precursor for heterojunction formation through in situ phase conversion, simplifying device fabrication while simultaneously improving photoresponse performance. First-principles calculations further corroborate that the robust built-in electric field at the heterojunction interface facilitates carrier separation. This work provides a simple and cost-effective strategy for developing high-performance, low-power-consumption self-powered infrared photodetectors.
10.1021_acscatal.6c02158: Alkaline water electrolysis is a promising route for hydrogen production, yet its widespread application is hindered by the sluggish kinetics of the oxygen evolution reaction (OER) and the insufficient durability of electrocatalysts. Herein, we investigate a pyrite-type high-entropy sulfide, (FeCoNiZnV)S 2, as a precatalyst for alkaline OER. Under anodic polarization, the material undergoes in situ surface reconstruction characterized by the preferential leaching of Zn and V species, the formation of sulfur vacancies, and the development of a defective multimetal oxyhydroxide layer. The resulting reconstructed phase, denoted as FeCoNiZnVOOH-S, exhibits an enlarged electrochemically active surface area and a tailored local coordination environment. As a result, the catalyst achieves an overpotential of 244 mV at 100 mA cm −2 in 1.0 M KOH. When employed as both anode and cathode in a two-electrode configuration, the electrolyzer delivers a cell voltage of only 1.52 V at 10 mA cm −2 and demonstrates stability for over 200 h at 1000 mA cm −2 in a flow-cell system. Post-operando analysis confirms that the reconstructed oxyhydroxide phase is preserved during prolonged electrolysis. This work underscores the critical role of dynamic surface reconstruction in high-entropy materials and offers a rational design strategy for developing robust OER electrocatalysts toward large-scale alkaline water electrolysis.
10.1039_d5ta00770d: An advanced catalyst drives innovation in zinc–air battery technology, delivering exceptional performance, stability, and efficiency with successfully powering a mobile phone.
10.1039_d6ta04118c: The in situ Li + -conductive piezoelectric LBO layer accelerates interface ion transport kinetics through continuous ion pathways and force–electric coupling and promotes the LiF/B-F-rich SEI, enabling high-current-density cycling of m-Si anodes.
